# Synthetic manuscript for a behavioral test

This is invented test material, not a real research manuscript. The results below are fixed inputs for a writing exercise. Do not add experiments or author facts.

## Current title

Integration of many advanced tools reveals a conserved stromal immune mechanism

## Current abstract

We used bulk transcriptomics, single-cell sequencing, spatial scoring, enrichment, network inference and virtual perturbation. Our study contains a mouse repeated-stress comparison and public human reproductive tissue profiles. The original mouse experiment included six control and six exposed animals. Single-cell profiling yielded 12,840 cells from all twelve animals. Stromal proliferation-marker-positive area decreased from 18.4% to 11.2% (adjusted P = 0.018). Collagen-positive area increased from 9.8% to 15.1% (adjusted P = 0.026). Relative NK-cell representation was lower but did not meet the prespecified multiple-testing threshold (FDR = 0.18). Within-state pseudobulk identified 86 differentially expressed genes in one NK state and 41 in another, using FDR below 0.05. A human reference included 12 disease and 18 control biopsies sampled across different cycle phases. Spatial observations came from a separate eight-donor study. Computational candidate scores were 5 for Candidate A, 5 for Candidate B and 4 for Candidate C. No functional intervention on these candidates was performed. All methods together prove a conserved regulatory axis that drives implantation failure.

## Results currently ordered

1. Comparison of computational tool outputs and tuning diagnostics.
2. Human cohort programme scores; mixed-cycle sampling.
3. Original mouse single-cell atlas, composition and within-state pseudobulk.
4. Tissue proliferation and collagen measurements.
5. Spatial programmes in the independent human reference.
6. Computational candidate scores.

## Methods available

The original mouse comparison used the animal as the independent unit. Pseudobulk was performed within prespecified cell states from raw counts. The significant-gene threshold was FDR below 0.05 within each state. Relative representation and tissue measurements used their own prespecified correction families. Human data were reanalysed separately. No human cycle-matched disease-effect test is supplied. There is no candidate perturbation experiment or measurement of absolute NK-cell number or immune function.
